> [!NOTE]

## 2026-10-27 Code Anatomy Reference Boundary

CK3 references: see mechanics-01-time-and-pulse.md:11-43, mechanics-02-character-rpg.md:125-173, mechanics-03-schemes.md:11-173, mechanics-04-war-and-combat.md:11-95, mechanics-05-economy.md:54-98, mechanics-06-vassals-court-council.md:11-95, mechanics-07-succession.md:182-209, mechanics-08-faith-culture.md:165-207, and internal-architecture-synthesis.md:117-126. Installation integrity, the full execution order, hot reload, and multiplayer/replay reuse of commands are unproven. CK3 figures are not Seoul rules. The in-depth research totals and clan formula are not adopted from summaries that remain in an independent-verification mismatch state. The queue in depth-04-war-and-binary.md:1317-1426,1628-1635 is for submission/insertion, and the actual consumption loop and damage formula remain unrecovered.

[Separation Contract Between Seoul Facts and Product Authority](/gdd/rules/game-logic-principles/)

Character sheets, calculations, and per-domain rules and situations are covered in the [Character and Domain Design Guide](/gdd/system-design/mechanism-design-index/). It is a design proposal that distinguishes the approved scope from alternatives not adopted.

> Source handoff: shared research index. Mentions of the local sources.json and raw-text packets are records from the time of research and do not mean that raw materials are included in this delivery. Missing IDs remain unconfirmed.
> This is an auto-generated document — it was derived from the internal repository research document (`Reference-Game-Mechanisms.md`), and prohibited terms have been replaced to meet the wiki's public release standards.

# Reference Game Mechanics Database

> This document is the **source of evidence** for the game design. It organizes mechanics confirmed from the wikis, manuals, and developer blogs of reference games, together with quotations from the original text, and makes it traceable which rules each game logic document adopted from which reference. The S-IDs in this document use a per-investigation source index and are separate from the existing Research-Sources list.
> 

## How to Use

- Each section follows the structure **Game → Mechanic → Source Evidence → Janseon Adoption**
- When citing this document from game logic documents (Campaign-Loop.md, etc.), use the format `[REF:geimmyeong-mekeonijeum]`
- When new research results come in, add them to the relevant game's section (append-only)
- **Combination rule**: If multiple games offer different solutions to the same problem, list them side by side as "options" and state Janseon's reason for its choice

v3 boundary: the "Janseon adoption" and "Janseon" items in this document and scope statements such as "three-station scope", "each of the three stations" and "three stations × B1/B2" are old-blueprint statements. Battle is replaced by Bible section 2.5 (owner decision D3) and v3 chapter 09 section 3: each army has one commander, who commands every squad of the army in a field battle, and individual resolution is used only for duels and hero fights. The old manual SRPG and the three-station scope are not current design. This paragraph does not mean implementation is complete.

---

## 1. Kenshi (K-System) — Wanderer Survival and Settlement Progression

> This is a prohibited term on the public wiki, so it is referred to as "K-System" only in internal design. Details: internal comprehensive research document §I.

### 1.1 Starting Conditions [REF:K-START]

- **13 starting scenarios**: each has a different combination of "deprivation" — lack of personnel / funds / equipment / faction relations. Poverty is not a single difficulty but several kinds of deprivation.
- **The player faction exists from the start**: under the faction name `Nameless`, it is a political actor even before settling. It is not the case that "you must settle to become a faction."
- **"You are not special"**: the world keeps running without the player. Enemies also fight each other.
- **Janseon adoption**: adopts the "Nameless Person" concept from Game-Thesis.md. **Additional design**: diversified starting scenarios (differentiated by deprivation axis).

### 1.2 Survival Pressure [REF:K-SURVIVAL]

- **Body**: per-body-part health. Arms and legs can be severed. Treatment requires time plus medical supplies. The early-game skill is choosing recoverable failures.
- **Food**: per-character hunger. Neglect leads to collapse → continued neglect leads to death.
- **Defeat ≠ game over**: instead of dying, you are sold into slavery or robbed by bandits and survive. Recovering after failure is the core loop.
- **Janseon adoption**: the injury system ("serious injury → HP reduction") is adopted. Slavery/plunder on defeat is a non-goal, but the spirit of "recovering after defeat" is adopted.

### 1.3 Wanderer → Settlement [REF:K-SETTLEMENT]

- **Three states**: ① full nomad (camping) ② house in a city (temporary base) ③ outdoor outpost (production base). Each has different event conditions.
- **Timing of settlement**: determined not by date but by preparation (research, materials) and need (necessity of production).
- **After settling**: diplomacy, invasions, and taxes arise. Rights grow, but so do responsibilities.
- **Janseon adoption**: three stages: `Wanderer → Facility Access Holder → Optional Station Operator`. **Settling is not a mandatory promotion.**

### 1.4 Unaffiliated Economy [REF:K-NOMAD]

- **Nomads are also political actors**: faction relations and reputation exist. They are not expelled from cities (except for crimes).
- **Economic sources**: plunder, merchants, commissions, mining. Technology can be acquired even without a base (using books + research bench).
- **Janseon adoption**: "preparation/recovery/settlement possible even without a fixed base" — solved through the facility access concept.

### 1.5 Why "Starting from Nothing" Is Fun [REF:K-WHY-FUN]

- **Self-generated goals**: not tutorial objectives but a natural chain of needs: "hungry → food → money → work."
- **Failure points**: not knowing where to go or what to do due to a lack of early information. A game with no rest because of constant threats.
- **Janseon**: the commission board is the starting point of the needs chain. Constant threats are eased by the rhythm of round trips between expeditions and the base.

> Details: internal comprehensive research document §II.

### 2.1 Origins [REF:BB-ORIGINS]

- **15 Origins**: Each one is not a starting bonus but a **long-term rule for the company** (hiring limits, starting equipment, special abilities). `Sellsword` is not a standalone origin.
- **Janseon**: Refer to this when diversifying starting scenarios along a "scarcity axis."

### 2.2 Economic Pressure Loop [REF:BB-ECONOMY]

- **Wages**: Paid daily in crowns. If you can't pay, morale drops → desertion. **Money buys freedom, and keeping that freedom means earning it again.**
- **Food**: Consumed daily. Each type has its own spoilage rate.
- **Repairs, Medicine, Ammunition**: The upkeep cost of equipment is a constant pressure.
- **Janseon adoption**: The supply system. **Difference**: In Janseon, supplies are consumables rather than currency. The "pressure consumed on every expedition" is the same.

### 2.3 Roster ≠ Deployment [REF:BB-ROSTER]

- **Roster**: All squad members (capable of growth). **Deployment**: The members sent into battle.
- **Replacing the wounded**: The wounded rest on the roster while reserve members take the field in their place.
- The current target for troop and deployment size is undecided.

### 2.4 World Evolution and Crises [REF:BB-CRISES]

- **4 Crises**: Noble War, Undead Invasion, Orc Invasion, and Holy War (Blazing Deserts). Crises are not backdrops but **changes to the hiring market and supply lines**.
- **Contract type changes**: During a crisis, certain contracts increase or decrease.
- **Micro-scale world changes**: Settlement states (destroyed/occupied/liberated) change at the level of individual settlements.
- **Janseon adoption**: The crisis system in Campaign-Progression.md. **Design needed**: Crisis types, triggers, and the minimum implementation within the scope of the three stations.

### 2.5 Settlements [REF:BB-SETTLEMENTS]

- **City**: Large. Market, armory, training ground, temple. **Town**: Small. Basic market. **Fortress**: Military. Barracks.
- **Linking other people's cities and using them as your own base**: Even without settling down, the settlement network serves as the company's base.
- **Janseon adoption**: Facilities differ by station. **Design needed**: A list of facilities for each of the three stations.

### 2.6 Retinue [REF:BB-RETINUE]

- **18 non-combat retinue members**: A way for the company to develop without buildings. Merchants, scouts, tailors, etc.
- **Janseon adoption**: To be reviewed later — a support-personnel system for non-combatants.

### 2.7 Terrain Costs [REF:BB-TERRAIN]

- **Movement AP**: Flat terrain 2 AP, rough terrain 3 AP, swamp 4 AP, elevation change +1 AP.

## 3. First Comparison Target — Character-Driven Grand Strategy

### 3.1 Character Presence [Ref: Characters]

- **Persistent portraits**: The top bar always shows portraits, traits, stress, and resources.
- **Character cards**: Trait tooltips, opinions, relationships, secrets.

### 3.2 Choice Transparency [Ref: Choices]

- **Event options**: Each choice shows its cost/effect/probability in advance. Distinguishes Will Happen / Has Happened.
- **Nested tooltips**: Hover over a value → a tooltip showing how that value is calculated (why is it this value?).
- **Janseon adoption**: The three choices (cost/effect/risk) on Encounter Screen 7 plus the "Why not?" tooltip correspond to this.

### 3.3 Map Information Modes [Ref: Map]

- **Map modes**: Switch colors by type of information, such as territory/diplomacy/religion/culture.
- **Janseon adoption**: The "Information Mode" on Strategic Route Map S — toggles between display of spheres of influence/transit rights/threat level.

### 3.4 Warning/Issue System [Ref: Issues]

- **Blocking warnings**: A red indicator next to the button when an action is unavailable.
- **Non-blocking issues**: A "Notice N" list. Old warnings disappear automatically.
- **Janseon adoption**: The "Notice 1 · a party member injured" badge on the Base Hub corresponds to this.

---

- **Linear stages**: No free world map. Progress is made by following the story.
- **Janseon**: Not adopted (Janseon pursues free movement). However, refer to the structure in which an expedition's "objective" is tied to the story.

- **Clickable city map**: A city screen with facility selection (shop/inn/training ground).
- **Janseon adoption**: The "facility selection" structure of the Base Hub corresponds to this. However, walking around the city is not adopted.

- **Intermission screen**: Class, skill, and item setup. Dialogue events.
- **Character-driven dialogue**: Gain information by selecting keywords.
- **Janseon adoption**: The "Dialogue" and "Equipment" functions of the Base Hub correspond to this.

---

### 5.1 Manual Tactical Commands [REF:FE-COMMAND]

- **Unit → Command → Target → Confirm/Cancel**: Show movement range → select tile → action menu → attack preview → confirm.
- **Cancel costs nothing**: No state changes during preview.

---

## 6. Triangle Strategy — Choice and Conviction

### 6.1 Persuasion and Voting [REF:TS-VOTE]

- **Gather information → Persuade → Vote**: You must gather information before the conversation to raise the persuasion success rate.
- **Conviction system**: Choices accumulate toward convictions (Liberty/Morality/Utility) → unlocks dialogue options.
- **Janseon adoption**: The structure in which encounter choices accumulate into relationships and reputation corresponds to this. The conviction system is to be reviewed later.

---

## 7. Questions the Janseon Design Has Not Yet Answered

This list was found during the reference research but has not yet been reflected in the Janseon design.

---

---

> 2024 main entry. Detailed study: `.omo/evidence/gameplay-rubric-6d3fe97/ui-reference/extended-refs-structure.md` §8. §8-12 below distinguish [Document] directly reviewed materials / [Inference] structural interpretation / [Proposed Application] unimplemented Janseon design. No direct gameplay or video verification corresponding to [Observation] was performed. Sources S140-S165 are linked in `sources.json`.

### 8.1 Field, Operation, and Engagement [REF:UO-MAPS]

- [Document] The game links a field where you explore, talk, and gather via the area lane, a stage where you command multiple units in real time or paused, and an engagement that runs automatically according to pre-set tactics after contact. The field also has a day/night clock, and stages have a time limit and base defense. [S140; S141 pp.12,16,28,37]
- [Inference] There are two maps for issuing movement orders (travel and operation), and counting the engagement display makes three functional surfaces. Do not confuse the five nations or the total number of stages with the number of map types. [S140-S141]
- [Application Proposal] Strengthen Janseon's travel→battle→settlement round trip, but there is no need to add a separate automatic-engagement screen. [S141; S165]

### 8.2 Separation of Valor, Honors, and Renown [REF:UO-RESOURCES]

- [Document] Valor is earned by defeating enemies on the battlefield, liberating facilities, and so on, and is spent on sorties and battlefield skills. Honors are earned from quests/deliveries and spent on hiring, expanding formations, and promotions, while Renown unlocks features according to rank. They are different resources. [S141 pp.18,21,28,30]
- [Document] AP is used for active skills during an engagement, and PP for conditional reaction skills. Stamina affects operational endurance after an engagement, and movement is impossible at 0. The Korean wiki's sentence "defenseless at 0" conflicts with a correction in the same document, so it is not equated with being defenseless while resting. [S141 pp.28,37; S142 §7.4/§8]
- [Application Proposal] Do not merge combat AP, daily supply, and organizational growth qualifications into a single abstract resource. However, do not add every resource type from the original game to Janseon either. [S141; S165]

### 8.3 Up to 5 characters in 6 slots: roles, targets, and order [REF:UO-FORMATION]

### 8.4 Liberation → Restoration → Resource recovery [REF:UO-LIBERATION]

- [Document] After liberation, you can use the facility and restore it by delivering gathered goods. If a garrison soldier is assigned, you receive funds and nearby gathered goods each time a later stage is completed. A character stationed as a garrison soldier can still sortie. [S141 pp.18,20]
- [Inference] A garrison soldier does not carry the same opportunity cost as the dedicated administrative personnel in Shinsei/Romance of the Three Kingdoms. Liberation does not immediately mean autonomous state warfare or tax management. [S141 p.20; S142 §7.1]
- [Application Proposal] Separate station liberation from facility reactivation, but design separately how the absence of a local manager on an expedition affects operations in Janseon. [S165]

### 8.5 Conditional recruitment [REF:UO-RECRUIT]

- [Document] The official materials describe more than 60 unique characters. They distinguish story companions, side quests, battlefield conversations with specific characters, delayed effects of past decisions, arena challenges, and separate generic mercenary hiring. [S140-S144]
- [Document] Hilda requires completion and field acceptance after a battlefield conversation with Prim, and whether Gamel was released early on affects his joining late in the game. The review's 64 characters and the wiki's maximum of 71 are recorded as differences in counting scope, and the total number of recruits is not confirmed. [S142-S144]
- [Application Proposal] Do not hand out character joining automatically like loot; tie it to relationships, earlier choices, and missions. [S144; S165]

## 9. Bannerlord (Mount & Blade 2) — Changes in political standing within the same clan

> Base single-player structure. War Sails and mods excluded. Cross-checked against launch reviews, subsequent official patches, and the dedicated wiki; it does not guarantee every latest perk, daily wage, or founding condition. See detailed research §9. [S145-S153]

### 9.1 Unaffiliated → Mercenary → Vassal → Kingdom [REF:MB-PROGRESSION]

- [Document] A clan includes characters, family, companions, and multiple parties, and a kingdom includes multiple clans. According to the wiki, you gain mercenary status at T1/Renown 50 and vassal status at T2/Renown 150. The campaign has a framework of family and main quests, while Sandbox omits it. [S146-S147; S151 §5]
- [Document] A mercenary's influence is tied to contract income, and a vassal takes part in fiefs, policies, and army mobilization. An independent clan's holding of territory is distinguished from declaring a kingdom. The official e1.7.0 announcement describes founding through a governor dialogue, so the old guide claiming the Dragon Banner quest is the only way to found a kingdom is not adopted. [S149; S152]
- [Inference] This sequence is not a mandatory chapter list but a path for learning authority. BB is also a free sandbox, but its persistent subject is a mercenary company, whereas in Bannerlord even the clan's national role changes. [S97; S106; S146-S149]
- [Application Proposal] Janseon translates this into an authority transition of service contract → passage/supply agreement → operations consignment → optional self-governance. [S165]

### 9.2 Troop types, wages, supplies, and growth [REF:MB-PARTY]

- [Document] Promotion of regular soldiers differs from the individual perk growth of heroes. Cavalry promotion additionally consumes horses/warhorses. Daily wages, food, the morale effects of food variety, and injuries and flight from battle create the burden of an expedition. [S148; S151 §3.2/§4/§5.6]
- [Document] There are 6 attribute groups × 3 skills = 18 skills; they gain experience through use, and attribute/focus points adjust learning efficiency and range. Perks are chosen at skill tiers. Scouting, logistics, medical, and engineering roles require different competencies. [S147-S148]
- [Inference] Focus points are not money that instantly buys skill levels. The growth path is which character you actually assign to which task. [S148]
- [Application Proposal] Janseon's specialist personnel must change a party's endurance through restoration, transport, and medical work, beyond combat strength. [S165]

### 9.3 World map, fiefs, armies, and sieges [REF:MB-KINGDOM]

- [Document/Inference] There are three functional surfaces: an integrated strategy/travel map on which parties move, a local exploration space, and direct combat. Local interactions can also be handled through menus. Korean sources describe 84 days per year, but the actual conversion to seconds and the auto-pause boundaries of every menu are unverified. [S145-S146; S151 §7; S153]
- [Document] A fief is not automatically owned just by contributing to a siege; an allocation vote or the ruler's decision intervenes. The governor, facilities, food, prosperity, loyalty, security, and the safety of connected villages matter. [S146; S151 §6]
- [Document] With influence you can call other clans' parties into an army and replenish cohesion. Calling your own clan's parties is an exception to the influence cost. A siege involves preparing camps/equipment on the map and then moves into direct combat with walls, gates, ladders, and siege equipment. [S149; S151 §4.2/§6.2]
- [Application Proposal] Refer to defensive responsibility, dispersal of companions, and blockades of connected areas, but do not add large-scale first-person action combat. [S165]

### 9.4 Workshops and caravans [REF:MB-ECONOMY]

- [Document] Direct trade exploits regional price differences. Workshops are tied to raw materials → products and to local demand/competition, while caravans are tied to the risks of actual movement, trading, escort, and capture. The timing of caravan daily wages also differs from that of trade revenue. [S146; S150-S151]
- [Document] Launch reviews point out the limitation that workshops/caravans explain the causes of their profits poorly and offer shallow direct operational choices. "Having economic features" and "managing every business in depth" are separate matters. [S146]
- [Application Proposal] Show Janseon's production facilities/transport crews not as fixed interest but as profit and loss from raw materials, routes, managers, and operating costs. [S165]

## 10. Nobunaga's Ambition (信長の野望) — Shinsei's personnel and military supply, and Tenshouki's growth

> The Shinsei 2022 Japanese main-game manual is used as the primary source. The separate siege and defensive strongpoints in the current English Awakening/PK manual are separated out as expansion rules. Tenshouki is part of the PC series, and SFC exceptions are marked. See detailed research §10. [S154-S156]

### 10.1 Districts, castles, roads, and time [REF:NA-MAPS]

- [Document] Districts lie beneath the 72 provinces, and a castle becomes the center of troops and provisions for its district. A corps is an organization that groups multiple castles and delegates to them. Geographic divisions and administrative organization are not treated as the same hierarchy. [S154 3200/4200/8500]
- [Document/Inference] On the national map you handle domestic affairs, marching, contact battles, and sieges, and in a separate field battle you command units and retreat routes in real time. The main game has two map types, strategy and field battle, and the expansion's sieges are not counted retroactively. [S154 3300/4100/7300/7400; S155]
- [Document] You can adjust running/paused time; marching consumes provisions daily, income arrives at the start of each month, and merit evaluations occur every three months. This differs from Tenshouki's seasonal turns. [S154 3300/7100/8600]

### 10.2 Status, titles, and fief assignments [REF:NA-DELEGATION]

- [Document] The roles of a magistrate of directly held land, a lord of another castle, a castle lord, and a corps commander are different. A status raised through merit unlocks the positions one may hold. Lower statuses gain experience as magistrates, and the freedom to reassign lords/castle lords is also opened by the system reform policy. [S154 3200/5100/8100]
- [Document] Giving a low position to a high status can lower loyalty. Low loyalty carries the risk of defection, early surrender of a castle, and unauthorized withdrawal, while ability and compatibility affect development and a castle's strength. A district without a manager is not developed. [S154 3200/4300/5100]
- [Inference] The growth loop is territorial expansion → new positions → rewarding meritorious retainers → increased development/strength. A shortage of talent is a real bottleneck to expansion. [S154 5100/8600]
- [Application Proposal] Separate the station master, facility manager, and patrol command roles, and display vacancies in managers and the results of delegation. [S165]

### 10.3 Economy and war preparation [REF:NA-ECONOMY]

- [Document] Farmland/irrigation → koku → provisions and troops; markets/merchant towns → gold income. Unlike the gold tribute, provisions are stock held per castle. Effort is tied up in tasks and recovers after completion, and policies have a preparation period and monthly upkeep. [S154 4100/4200/5100/8100]
- [Document] Designating a target halts the lord's domestic affairs and switches to military preparation. A combat-ready state increases strength and carried provisions. Autonomous construction under the castle-town policy differs from direct construction in speed/cost. [S154 5300/7100]
- [Application Proposal] Include in mobilization costs not only the supplies used on deployment but also the halted production and local personnel. [S165]

### 10.4 Units, sieges, and prestige [REF:NA-WAR]

- [Document] The castle lord and the lords under him shape a unit's abilities. Cavalry/matchlock LV is an attack effect depending on facilities, policies, and traits, and is not the same as Tenshouki's exclusive troop-type choice. Road width and the number of days of provisions limit deployment. [S154 4200/7100]
- [Document] In the main game, sieges involve encirclement/assault and a durability contest, and in field battles victory comes not only by annihilation but also through total morale, retreat routes, and defeating the daimyo. Prestige can even change nearby allegiance, diplomacy, and loyalty. [S154 7200/7300/7400]
- [Application Proposal] Refer to the causality in which tactical results affect cooperation/passage at adjacent stations, but do not unconditionally award entire territories on a single victory. [S165]

### 10.5 Tenshōki's Talent, Education, and Corps [REF:NA-TENSHOKI]

- [Document] 214 castles on PC / 120 castles on SFC. Strategy runs on one-season turns and corps action points, and a mass battle involves up to 9 surrounding castles. Current Politics, Combat, and Strategy stats are separated from talent limits, and characters grow through practical work, education, and war. Troop-type aptitude and the procurement of warhorses and matchlocks also change military strength. [S156 §2.1-2.5]
- [Document] Outside the 1st Corps there are autonomy and policy settings, loyalty costs for dismissal/disbandment, and a risk of corps commanders becoming independent. Gold, rice, castle development, and merchant trade were confirmed, but the exact income seasons and formulas for agriculture/commerce are unconfirmed. [S156 §2.5-2.8]
- [Inference/Application Proposal] The fast feedback of growth and multi-castle conquest is appealing, but explosive combat growth can make non-combat characters meaningless. Janseon should provide skill paths that remain valid for field recovery, medicine, and transport. [S156 §2.5; S165]

## 11. Taikō Risshiden (太閤立志伝) — Separation of Livelihood, Status, and Command Authority

> 5 The baseline is the official DX manual, out of the original 2004 version and DX 2022. The official 960 characters are the full pool of playable characters, not everyone unlocked from the start. Detailed research §11. [S157-S160]

### 11.1 Career Advancement Is Not a Single Forced Tree [REF:TR-CAREER]

- [Document] Hideyoshi's rise is the motif, but the goals differ among warriors, merchants, ninja, and pirates, and among swordmasters, tea masters, physicians, and blacksmiths. One can start as a rōnin or as a character with an existing post, and "peasant → Kampaku" is not a common level tree. [S157; S158 1200; S159 4200/5160]
- [Document] Below the rank of Karō, one carries out the lord's orders; from castle lord upward, one opens direct councils and assigns work to subordinates. A provincial lord decides on multiple castles and transport, and a daimyo decides on diplomacy, the direction of conquest, and requests from other occupational factions. Independence/succession differs from simple automatic XP promotion. [S159 5100/5130/5160]
- [Application Proposal] Set livelihood skill, organizational rank, and facility operating authority as separate axes, so that a medic can achieve the feat of running a clinic without becoming a general. [S165]

### 11.2 Deadlines and Return Reports [REF:TR-TIME]

- [Document] The warrior council is held on days 1-5 of odd-numbered months: choose a mission → carry it out → report to the lord within the deadline → merit. In spare time one earns money, takes up apprenticeships, and socializes. Securing the mission item alone does not complete the report. [S159 5100]
- [Document] Ninja/pirates attend within one month after an irregular summons, and merchants hold councils at the start of odd-numbered months. Stipends go into the home strongbox at the start of each month. Travel/training/rest create opportunity costs in the schedule. [S158 3100/3200; S159 4200-4500/5200-5400]
- [Application Proposal] For Janseon's transport, treatment, and recovery requests, distinguish between task completion, the return report, and personal time until the next job. [S165]

### 11.3 Apprenticeship, Connections, and Cards [REF:TR-SKILLS]

- [Document] Distinguish the 5 abilities, 16 skills, and 6 card categories. Apprenticeship is tied to characters/facilities with high skills and to relationship/item conditions, and per the official description one can learn up to Level 4. Minigames and automatic handling for training/tasks differ between versions. [S158 3300/3400; S160 §3]
- [Document] Growing close through gifts, tea ceremonies, and sparring opens access to employment/apprenticeship/enrollment/recruitment. Merit, notoriety, titles, and court ranks are axes separate from intimacy. Protagonist cards unlock the next playable character, and not every skill card becomes shared combat power in the next playthrough. [S158 3200/3400/3600; S159 5100/5160/5500]
- [Application Proposal] Link growth to journeys to visit teachers and experts, and to practical work at livelihood sites. [S165]

### 11.4 Non-Ruling Paths and Personal Narratives [REF:TR-PATHS]

- [Document] Merchants run branch shops, sales routes, and commercial privileges; ninja/pirates operate separate bases, patron daimyo, and territories. Swordmasters pursue schools/dojos/disciples, tea masters pursue tea rooms/tea gatherings, physicians pursue herbs, pharmaceuticals, prescriptions, and treatment reputation, and blacksmiths pursue skill acquisition, raw materials, and weapon crafting. [S159 4300-5800]
- [Document] A faction occupation and a path-of-the-way occupation can be held at the same time, but only one workshop can be opened at home. Duels and mass battles are also separate, and in a mass battle one commands either one's own unit or the entire corps depending on status. [S158 1200/3500/3600]
- [Inference/Application Proposal] "What kind of person one has lived as" should lead to "who has gained the authority to entrust what work to whom." Not every success should be converted into military unification. [S158-S159; S165]

## 12. Romance of the Three Kingdoms (三國志) — 14's Land, Officers in Charge, and Supply Lines

> 2020 main game, Ruler mode. Distinguish it from titles where you play any officer, such as Romance of the Three Kingdoms 8 REMAKE, and do not use the modifier "latest 2026 release." Detailed research §12-14. [S161-S164]

### 12.1 Ruler Mode, HEX, and 10-Day Execution [REF:RTK-MAPS]

- [Document] Choose a faction that has the minimum number of cities, and secure HEX → regional core → city sphere. A corps is an organization to which several cities are delegated. If you lose all your cities, the faction collapses. [S162 2400/3100/3300]
- [Document/Inference] War and administration proceed on the same continuous map. Orders are decided in the strategy phase, then repeat as 10 days of progress → report, and ordinary orders cannot be changed while in progress. A month has 3 decades (xun), income comes at the start of the month, and supply occurs every decade. An officer designated as Adjutant intervening in tactic timing is distinguished as an exception. [S162 3200/3300/5300]
- [Application Proposal] Decide Janseon's time contract first, and do not mix real-time pause, scheduled execution, and manual tactical turns. [S165]

### 12.2 Talent Becomes Administrative Capacity [REF:RTK-OFFICERS]

- [Document] The official figures are 1000+ officers and 150+ traits, while Korean sources describe 1000 base historical officers, 46 cities, and 340 key points. Distinguish the scope of DLC/editing/historical counts. [S161; S163]
- [Document] Appoint officers in charge of regions, conscription, and training; if that person sorties or does other work, the effect is reduced. A region without an officer in charge suffers seasonal declines in development/public order. Leadership, Might, Intellect, Politics, and Charm each have different administrative uses. [S162 4200]
- [Document] The ruler's Focus sets the slots and cost limits of administrative departments, and the policies of the officers assigned there activate from the next decade. Military affairs have qualification and policy-cost exceptions. [S162 4100]
- [Application Proposal] Make ordinary specialist personnel, not just famous combatants, necessary for operating facilities and regions. [S165]

### 12.3 Development, Conscription, Formations, and Linkage [REF:RTK-WAR]

- [Document] Commerce/agriculture/barracks development of a region is separated from the officers in charge of city recruitment/training. Growing the troop count also increases consumption, and a shortage of provisions causes troop desertion/morale loss. [S162 4200]
- [Document] A sortie bundles the commander, formation, troops, tactic, objective, and engagement/pursuit/retreat policy. Formations distinguish mobility, occupation width, unit combat, and siege, and offices are tied to the cap on commanded troops. [S162 5100/6100/7100]
- [Document] If commanders on good terms are adjacent in the same corps and have no status ailments, linked abilities/tactics are strengthened. Traits create advantages and disadvantages and some restrictions on action settings. A hero is not merely a multiplier on troop numbers. [S162 5100]

### 12.4 Supply Lines and Version Boundaries of Diplomacy [REF:RTK-SUPPLY]

- [Document] The home city and units are connected through land controlled by your own side or allies, and distance and rough terrain affect consumption. If cut off, they suffer a large morale loss and movement/attack restrictions. The official guidance recommends dealing with Lü Bu/Zhang Liao through supply cutoffs, facilities, and tactics rather than a head-on fight. [S162 5100/7200]
- [Document] The main game's diplomacy list consists of friendship, alliance, cancellation, prisoner return, attack request, and surrender advice. A general marriage-alliance command has not been confirmed. Do not confuse historical marriage/spouse relationships with the general marriage diplomacy of Shinsei. [S162 6100; S154 6200]
- [Application Proposal] Refer to station/tunnel/transfer supply connections rather than HEX coloring. Let the restoration of passage, pumps, power, and medical transport change operational endurance. [S165]

### 12.5 The Five-Title Combination Principle [REF:RTK-SYNTHESIS]

- [Inference] Unicorn centers growth on expanding formation options through liberation, Bannerlord on a clan's political qualifications, Shinsei on delegating personnel affairs, Taikō Risshiden on an individual's career/authority, and Romance of the Three Kingdoms 14 on land, administration, and supply connections. They cannot all be bundled under the same "empty-handed → king" formula. [S141; S146-S149; S154; S158-S159; S162]
- [Application Proposal] Janseon's core is the BB expedition profit/loss + K survival/recovery sustainability + Taikō Risshiden's separation of livelihood and rank. Unicorn's matchups/formations, Shinsei's delegation, and the supply-cutoff connections of Romance of the Three Kingdoms reinforce that core. [S84; S89; S97; S102-S104; S141; S154; S158-S159; S162]
- [Application Proposal] Unicorn's "defenders can also sortie" and the dedicated-personnel costs of Shinsei/Romance of the Three Kingdoms are incompatible, so a choice must be made. For Janseon, we recommend proxy substitution or an operating-efficiency loss during expeditions, with the numbers and qualifications designed separately. The old blueprint's manual SRPG and three stations × B1/B2 contract were replaced by the field battle of Bible section 2.5 D3 and v3 chapter 09 section 3 (see the v3 boundary above), and this research changes neither that battle contract nor the occupation → stabilization → integration design. [S141 p.20; S154 5300; S162 4200; S165]

## 13. Capture and Recruitment — Separating Detention, Liberation, and Voluntary Joining

> Research: `st_01a0777a`, 2026-09-06. Details: `.omo/evidence/gameplay-rubric-6d3fe97/ui-reference/capture-recruit-system.md`. Sources S110–S129 are linked to `sources.json` in the same folder. **[Document]** is a static reading of wikis and version-pinned code materials, **[Inference]** is interpretation, and **[Application Proposal]** is an unimplemented design. The original game was not run and the Janseon runtime was not verified. [S119, S129]

### 13.1 K-System: Capture Is Not Gaining Control [REF:K-CAPTURE]

- **[Document: Original Text]** The Prisoner Cage detains a target by "first pick up the target" and then "select 'put in'". A single-person prison, shackles, and slave status are different states. Assassination is a stealth knockout, and the Prisoner Pole is also a restraint device, not a recruitment facility. [S110, S113]
- **[Document]** After liberation, outcomes split into fleeing, refusing liberation, temporarily following, and joining. Some unique prisoners join immediately, and raiders may free captives. Character despawn in prison is a documented bug, so it is not treated as a normal escape probability. [S111, S112, S113]
- **[Proposed Application]** Survival/securing is decided at B, evacuation at S, and joining at N. No control over combat or labor is granted during detention. [Basis: S113, S120, S126]

### 13.2 K-System: Personality, Eligibility, and Memory of Harm [REF:K-PRISONER-RECRUIT]

- **[Document: Original Text]** Slavery: "Players cannot own their own slaves." Purchasing is not ownership of private labor but a route where the person may join or leave after liberation. [S110]
- **[Document]** There is no universal rule of confine → feed/heal → trust gauge → join. The thresholds are personality, an available recruitment dialogue package, recruitment eligibility, and memories of past kidnapping or sale. A dialogue exists for reuniting with a savior, but the wiki also says the cause of the lifesaver tag being generated is uncertain. [S111, S112, S115]
- **[Document]** Personality consists of dialogue tags: Honorable/Traitorous/Smart/Dumb/Brave/Fearful/Maniacal. Fearful/Dumb are reluctant to escape, Brave/Traitorous tend to escape on their own, and Smart/Honorable have a path to following. Shek/Hive Prince are exceptions. The wiki's 41% is a conditional follow-up branch for characters who have already followed, not a join rate for all prisoners. [S111, S112]
- **[Document]** Playable Characters states that if `max(STR,DEX)+max(MeleeAttack,MartialArts)+max(MeleeDefense,Dodge)>=75`, general eligibility is not met, and it excludes Diplomat/Law Enforcer/Military/Trader. This conflicts with the STR+DEX+Toughness summary in Slavery, and some dialogues bypass the eligibility check. This is not directly verified in FCS. [S110, S115]
- **[Proposed Application]** Do not use personality solely as a hidden success rate; express it through reasons for demanding or refusing to join, such as protecting family, refusing to attack former comrades, or personal grudges. Food and treatment alone do not guarantee joining. [Basis: S111, S112, S115, S121]

### 13.3 K-System: Captive Economy and Duplicate Rewards [REF:K-CAPTIVE-ECONOMY]

- **[Document]** Handing over an ordinary slave pays 400c, and there is a separate Rebirth route with class restrictions. Bounties are settled with the issuing faction at full value for live capture or half for a corpse. Slave prices and bounties are not rewards that automatically stack on every captive. [S110, S114]
- **[Document]** Documented cases include gratitude/recruitment being blocked toward the person who sold you directly, bypassing memory of responsibility by enslaving through a third party, and a duplicate money/relationship bug from repeatedly submitting the same bounty target. Recruiting or discovering a particular escaped slave can trigger an attack on a Slave Capture base. [S110, S111, S114]
- **[Inference]** The choice between immediate income and long-term manpower investment is valid, but a loop of harm → rescue creates trust farming. The original perpetrator, transfer history, and reward exhaustion are needed. [S110, S111, S114]
- **[Proposed Application]** Initially, instead of a slave-selling market, offer only contracted bounties, handovers, and exchanges, and process custody transfer/payment once per character + commission ID. [Basis: S114, S123, S128]

### 13.4 Bannerlord: Regular Troops Are Conformity Throughput [REF:MB-PRISONER-RECRUIT]

- **[Document]** The provided Capture prisoners is a classic commission. The earlier game's 40% + Persuasion × 4%, 24-hour camp, and -3 morale are not cited as Bannerlord formulas. Companions are hired at taverns and Lords use an ability table, so a separate recruitment-formula source is needed. [S116, S117, S118]
- **[Document]** I read the official v1.2.12 API and the same-version commit `d345b5dfc42b0fbb06b8b4b48b96486ed86d0d2f` of a public decompilation. The official API has declarations only; the coefficients come from an unofficial code archive. It is not guaranteed to be the common official formula for all current distributions. [S119, S120]
- **[Document: Code]** Required amount per unit `K=(Level+6)^2-10`; the hourly base gain of the selected troop-type bundle is `10+0.05×Leadership`, rounded after perk adjustments. Recruitable count is `min(prisoner count, floor(troop-type XP/K))`. [S119]
- **[Document]** Each hour, starting from a random point, **only one** incomplete regular-troop bundle increases. It does not increase for every prisoner or every troop type at the same time. When recruitment is confirmed, XP and prisoner count decrease and member count increases. Heroes are excluded from regular-troop recruitment. [S119, S120]
- **[Document]** Charm and personal relationships are not direct terms in this regular-troop speed formula. The same-culture + Presence perk is a condition for exemption from the recruitment morale loss. Do not mix the regular -1 / bandit -2 morale and the Two Faced bandit exemption with the noble persuasion probability. [S119]
- **[Document]** A regular blunt hit returns survival 1 unless a special lethal-permitting flag is present. Other damage can also be survived as an injury through medicine, level, Doctor's Oath, and so on. The generalization that "only blunt weapons make prisoners" is wrong. [S122]
- **[Proposed Application]** Janseon should select the qualifications, consent, and contracts of a few individuals rather than mass-converting troop-type XP. Adopt the separation of prisoners/members and the evacuation and settlement costs. [Basis: S120, S126, S127]

### 13.5 Bannerlord: Defection of Noble Prisoners to a Clan [REF:MB-LORD-DEFECTION]

- **[Document: Original Text]** The 1.2.12 eligibility for the prisoner line "join us, and be set free." requires: the player to be the kingdom ruler, the target to be a clan leader, the current ruling clan to be excluded, and the prisoner to be in custody of the player's party or owned settlement; the CapturedLord/FreedHero context immediately after battle is excluded. The claim that "noble prisoners can never defect" is also wrong. [S121]
- **[Document]** Hesitations over trust, oaths, loyalty, policy, and interests are resolved through argument. Options and outcomes (success, critical success, failure, critical failure) vary with the skill/trait used, argument strength, relationship, and event ledger. After success, a separate clan-joining barter may be needed. A failed attempt on the same target/hesitation has a retry restriction within 1 week. [S121]
- **[Document]** Ransom is calculated from clan, wealth, number of fiefs, and perks, and noble escape is a daily check depending on location, number of guards, and perks. This is distinct from hourly escape when the regular-troop limit is exceeded. The clan/friend/faction/honor costs of peaceful release and execution are also separate. [S123]
- **[Inference]** Recruiting ordinary prisoners is a troop conversion, while noble defection is a change of affiliation of a political group. Explaining them with the same button/success rate breaks both the scale and the causality. [S119, S121, S123]
- **[Proposed Application]** Treat Janseon's major leaders as targets of political events rather than ordinary roster recruitment. Even characters in ordinary duty roles update vacancies and affiliation relationships, and their original faction as a whole does not automatically become an ally. [Basis: S121, S127]

### 13.6 BB: Exceptions to the Premise That There Is No Capture [REF:BB-CAPTURE-EXCEPTION]

- **[Document: Original Text]** Recruitment in the Game Guide is "In settlements for a fee" / "Via events for free". The baseline comparison centering on hiring markets is correct, but it is not exclusively city hiring. [S125]
- **[Document: Original Text]** Manhunters event: "You captured an Indebted after winning a battle". In Blazing Deserts, this origin lets you obtain one Indebted in a bad mood, or decline, under the conditions of an eligible human-versus-human victory/enemy retreat and an empty roster slot. This differs from generic capture that transfers a battlefield unit's abilities and equipment as they are. [S124]
- **[Document]** It also comes with 16 deployed / 25 owned, pressure on the Indebted ratio, a level 7 cap, and death upon being knocked down. Therefore **the premise that the whole of BB has no recruitment by capturing enemies is corrected.** [S124]
- **[Inference]** With basic hiring as the center, it is easy to price hiring costs, daily wages, and training losses independently and to preserve the reason to visit cities. Capture gives narrative continuity with the enemy but increases duplicate rewards of manpower, equipment, and loot, as well as state complexity. This is an interpretation, not a claim confirming undisclosed development intent. [S124, S125, S126]

### 13.7 Janseon: B Securing → W Evacuation → N Joining [REF:JS-CAPTURE-RECRUIT]

**[Proposed Application] The numbers below are new balance hypotheses, not implemented values.** For detailed state transitions, escape formulas, trust formulas, and accommodation scenarios, follow report §§11–20. [Basis: S126, S127, S128]

| Face/Stage | Proposed Rule | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B Subdue | Add a non-lethal melee command at 1 AP (hypothesis); a stable downed state at HP 0. Those seriously wounded by a lethal attack can survive with first aid within the time limit | [S113, S122, S128] |
| B Secure | Securing 1 AP, first aid 1 AP + 1 medical supply (hypothesis). After the last enemy, battlefield cleanup guarantees the option to evacuate; on a retreat, only targets carried to the exit | [S113, S120, S128] |
| W Evacuation | Initially 1 slot (hypothesis); an escort, a cart, and food are required. Competes with evacuating wounded allies; escape checks occur only in fixed segments/camp events | [S123, S126, S128] |
| N Facility | Own station not required, but usage rights to a friendly facility are needed. Determines treatment/release/contract handover/accommodation/joining conditions | [S110, S114, S123, S126] |
| N Joining | Requires all of: consciousness recovered + role transferred + independent reason to leave + demands resolved + trust 2 or higher + consent + capacity + contract fee | [S111, S115, S121, S127] |
| Roster | Detention end/joining processed once; injuries and equipment preserved. Broken promises go warning → conflict → renegotiation/departure, with no hidden daily betrayal dice | [S120, S121, S125, S128] |

- **[Proposed Application]** Trust is a -3..+3 hypothesis, -1 immediately after capturing a stranger enemy. Appropriate treatment is capped at +1 per whole event, and fulfilling guarantees/independence promises is separately required. Repeated food and treatment alone do not reach the joining threshold. Initial persuasion is condition-based, and tightened guarding prevents escape but does not build trust. [Basis: S110, S111, S114, S121]
- **[Document]** Starting-Presets states that Cast characters are randomly placed as starting companions through per-preset filters. Detailed execution rules for redrawing campaign candidates were not confirmed in the documents read. [S127]
- **[Proposed Application]** The starting draw, N regular hiring, and B capture/rescue all go through the same PersonId store and the shared recruitment eligibility/JoinRoster. Imprisoned or rostered characters are not duplicated as candidates at other stations or as enemies, and their names, abilities, relationships, and pasts are preserved. [Basis: S120, S127, S128]
- **[Proposed Application]** Store the original captor and transfer history, reward exhaustion per person + bounty ID, per-purpose RNG and event sequence numbers, and roster/detention ownership. Previews, menu round trips, and save/load do not advance time or dice. [Basis: S110, S114, S128]
- **[Proposed Application]** Slave markets, slave labor, general-purpose execution, and daily hidden loyalty dice are not adopted initially. Regular hiring is kept, and capture is left as an optional path. A fourth map surface for walking around prisons is not created. [Basis: S110, S121, S124, S125, S126]

### 13.8 Limits of the Evidence [REF:CAPTURE-EVIDENCE-LIMITS]

- **[Document]** The Bannerlord formulas are static data from 1.2.12. The latest HEAD has different recruitment eligibility, maritime conditions, and culture comparisons, so they were not mixed in. The full K-System FCS tree and the 41% cross-version commonality were not directly verified. [S112, S115, S119, S129]
- **[Document]** Workshop HTTP 200 internal rate-limit errors, some guide 404/403 responses, and empty shells were not used as positive evidence. [S129]
- **[Proposed Application]** Subdue/transport/join/roster full/refuse/death/escape, save restoration, and prevention of duplicate settlement are presented as future acceptance scenarios. Janseon's proposed values and actual UI behavior have not yet been verified. [Basis: S128, S129]

## 14. Open-Source Implementation References — Mechanisms Read from Source (2026-09-17)

> We examined 15 titles at the source level from the owner-designated open-source catalog (github.com/bobeff/open-source-games). If the commercial game research (§1–13) asks about design intent, this section asks about implementation numbers. The full detailed text is in the repository at `RESEARCH/canon-reference/open-source-games-mechanisms.md` — every load-bearing fact carries a source path, access date (2026-09-17), and a short verbatim quote, and anything unconfirmed remains marked UNVERIFIED. The current goal is individual combat adjudicated per character.

### 14.1 OpenXcom — Morale Contagion and Reaction Initiative [REF:OS-OXC-MORALE]

- **[Document: Code]** A hit is not a binomial roll but a deviation-based one — `deviation = RNG(0,100) - accuracy*100`, followed by aim-point pushing. Kneeling ×1.15, imperfect two-handed grip ×0.8, injury modifier `max(10, 25*HP/maxHP + 75 - 10*fatalWounds)`. src/Battlescape/Projectile.cpp
- **[Document: Code]** Morale ranges 0–100, and the loss when hit is `100*(damage*bravery coefficient)/command modifier`. Death contagion: killing an enemy +20, friendly-fire death -2000/mod, rank-based modifiers 110–150. Panic probability `100 - 2*morale`, with +15 after resolution to prevent chain reactions. src/Savegame/BattleUnit.cpp·SavedBattleGame.cpp
- **[Document: Code]** Reaction fire score = `reaction stat × remaining TU/max TU` — an initiative queue based on the remaining ratio. Vision separates an absolute cap of 20 tiles from 9 tiles at night, and smoke is converted into optical distance. src/Battlescape/TileEngine.cpp
- **[Document: Code]** When research is assigned, the actual cost varies as `cost × RNG(50,150)%`, and end-of-month funding rises or falls 5–20% based on country satisfaction (activity/10 vs. threat/20). The RNG is a single global xorshift — a cautionary example for Janseon's stream contract. src/Basescape/ResearchInfoState.cpp
- **[Proposed Application]** Consider the morale contagion, command modifier, and panic recovery constants as the numerical skeleton of the morale system. This is an unadopted research proposal, and this revision introduces no thresholds or constants. The turn structure is not adopted.

### 14.2 OpenPanzer — Probability-Free Combat Table, Entrenchment, and Core Roster [REF:OS-OP-COMBAT]

- **[Document: Code]** Combat has no RNG: `kF = atk-def; if kF>4 then 4+(2kF-8)/5; +6; clamp(1,19); kills = round((5*kF*strength+50)/100)`. js/gamerules.js
- **[Document: Code]** Entrenchment snaps to a terrain baseline and then stacks per tick (`next = 9*level+4`), capped at terrain+5, reset to 0 on movement and -1 when hit. Urban infantry vs. vehicles are calculated twice. js/unit.js·prototypes.js
- **[Document: Code]** Campaign core roster: experience is kept while HP, ammo, and entrenchment are reset — the opposite pole from Janseon's persistent injuries (explicitly not adopted). A single prestige wallet (flag +20, objective +50). js/map.js
- **[Proposed Application]** A candidate formula for siege preview adjudication that preserves seed determinism.

### 14.4 Ancient Beast — Typed Damage Vectors and Status Data [REF:OS-AB-DAMAGE]

- **[Document: Code]** Damage is a `{type: value}` vector, `value×(1+(attack-defense/area+affinity Δ)/100)`, with a total floor of 1, and pure damage bypasses this. Damage also reduces endurance separately from HP. src/damage.ts
- **[Document: Code]** Status effect = trigger string + list of alterations patches (a serializable object including stacks, lifetime, and removal triggers). src/effect.ts·creature.ts
- **[Document: Code]** Initiative queue `init×500 - id` — ties are broken by a stable id rather than by RNG. Summoning cost `size+level`, and death drops are permanent stat patches with no expiry. src/creature.ts·drop.ts

### 14.5 Cataclysm: DDA — Scale Separation, Relationship Integers, and the Need Clock [REF:OS-CDDA-OPINION]

- **[Document: Code]** Three-layer coordinates (tile / submap 12×12 / OMT 24×24, overmap 180²). Subways and roads use `overmap_connection {terrain, locations, basic_cost}` — with edge costs (road 0, forest 20, swamp 40, water 120), so pathing prefers low-cost routes. data/json/overmap/overmap_connections.json
- **[Document: Code]** NPCs outside the reality bubble (132²) catch up with a cap of `min(elapsed, 2 days)` (30 min → 5 min → 1 turn buckets), and groups move across the overmap as lightweight entities and are promoted when they enter the bubble. src/npc.cpp·overmap.cpp — a second real-world confirmation of the K-System bubble design.
- **[Document: Code]** Relationships use six integer axes `trust/fear/value/anger/owed/sold` plus personality int8 ±10. Hostility threshold `anger ≥ 20 + fear - aggression`. If a faction's `likes_u < -10`, its members become hostile. Ally trust rises +1 with some probability each hour (penalty = anger + appraisal + fear + hunger + thirst + injury). src/npc.cpp·doc/JSON/FACTIONS.md
- **[Document: Code]** Needs are settled in bulk every 5-minute tick as `rate×n`, with subjective hunger separated from stored calories, and water at 250 ml per 5 minutes. A model for settling expedition consumption. src/character_body.cpp·stomach.cpp
- **[Document: Code]** Recipes use nested AND/OR arrays with per-step checks, and `unattended` steps run on wall-clock time (the process advances while the party is away). Prices use a per-faction `{markup, premium, fixed_adj}` overlay plus a per-NPC debt (owed) ledger. doc/JSON/ITEM_CRAFT_AND_DISASSEMBLY.md·npctrade.cpp
- **[Proposed Application]** A first prototype for tunnel edge costs in the 334-station graph, lazy generation of station interiors, integer relationship axes for the cast, and unattended processes at stations.

### 14.6 Unciv — Sequential Turn Pipeline and State-Hash RNG [REF:OS-UNCIV-TURN]

- **[Document: Code]** City growth `15 + 8(pop-1) + floor((pop-1)^1.5)`, -1 population when food is negative, carry-over cap 95%. core/.../CityPopulationManager.kt
- **[Document: Code]** Yield is applied in the order: source stat tree → % tree → production priority → conversion (1/4) → upkeep. CityStats is recalculated every turn without being stored. core/.../CityStats.kt
- **[Document: Code]** Turns cycle sequentially (human → AI chain → human), and "Next Turn" is gated by undecided choices. Multiplayer exchanges save files sequentially (not lockstep). core/src/com/unciv/logic/GameInfo.kt·docs/Other/Multiplayer.md
- **[Document: Code]** Movement 1.0 = internal fixed-point 30, railroad 0.1 = heuristic cap, passing through a zone of control = sentinel 100 (consumes all remaining movement). core/.../FixedPointMovement.kt·MovementCost.kt
- **[Document: Code]** Probability rolls use `stateBasedRandom(caller, seed)` — a hash of (caller, turn, entity id) that blocks rerolling after a reload. Saves store only name references. models/ruleset/unique/GameContext.kt — the closest real implementation of the PurposeRng contract.

### 14.7 Freeciv — Phase Mode, Sliders, and Handicaps [REF:OS-FCV-PHASES]

- **[Document: Code]** Turns and phases are separate: `phase_mode` determines concurrent (1 phase, order shuffled every turn) / alternating (number of players) / team alternating, and it is stored in the save to prevent repeated side effects on load. server/srv_main.c
- **[Document: Code]** City trade is distributed as integers across science/luxury/tax percentages (summing to 100), with a hard override of luxury 100 under anarchy. common/city.c
- **[Document: Code]** AI difficulty is data: a handicap bit vector + fuzzy (a boolean flipped with probability in thousandths) + a research cost multiplier. Even the highest difficulty keeps government constraints (H_RATES) — blocking through constraints rather than hidden buffs. ai/difficulty.c

### 14.8 VCMI·fheroes2 — Heroes, Armies, and Campaign Carry-Over [REF:OS-VCMI-CARRYOVER]

- **[Doc: Code]** Stack = `{taip, su}` (VCMI 7 slots, fheroes2 5 slots). Map strength is the sum of `AIValue×su` plus the hero coefficient `sqrt((1+0.05ATK)(1+0.05DEF))`, a single scalar for display and diplomacy. lib/mapObjects/army/
- **[Doc: Code]** Movement: the daily budget is based on the slowest unit in the party (VCMI table 1300~2000, fheroes2 enum 1000~1500), with terrain cost and a pathfinding discount (swamp 175→100), and roads at 75/65/50 (VCMI) and 75 (fheroes2). config/gameConfig.json·maps/ground.cpp
- **[Doc: Code]** Campaign carryover keep-flags: VCMI uses per-axis keep booleans plus a creature allow list, while fheroes2 uses a minimal army snapshot. This is the prototype of the Janseon (lingering thread) cast carryover contract (per-axis flags for injuries, relationships, and values). lib/campaign/CampaignState.h
- **[Doc: Code]** RNG: VCMI uses `minstd_rand` with state serialization and per-hero streams, while fheroes2 uses PCG32 with a seed queue stored on the hero (deterministic level-ups with no live rolls). lib/CRandomGenerator.h·src/engine/rand.h
- **[Doc: Code]** Town: one construction per day, and a weekly growth aggregator (VCMI base + castle bonus + …, fheroes2 Well +2 / Well2 +8, neutral half). lib/mapObjects/CGTownInstance.cpp·castle.cpp

### 14.9 OpenNefia — Favor Thresholds and the Relationship Duality [REF:OS-ONEFIA-IMPRESSION]

- **[Doc: Code]** Favor is an integer + named thresholds (0/10/25/50/53/75/100/150/200/300); the displayed tier is a pure function. Gain diminishing returns `delta×100/(50+L³)`; conversation consumes Interest(100) + 8-hour refresh. Dialog/DialogSystem.cs
- **[Doc: Code]** Relationship is an enum `Enemy-3..Ally10` + a sparse map of personal overrides; combat aggro is a separate integer (discovery 30, ally damage 5, -1 per turn) — separating 'whose side' from 'who right now' matches the Janseon cast/combat separation. Factions/FactionComponent.cs·VanillaAI
- **[Doc: Code]** Shop `itemCount = min(80, 20+raengkeu/2)`, restocking is a 24-hour date trigger. At karma -30 the guards turn hostile immediately — separation of layers between personal relationship and global reputation. Shopkeeper/ShopkeeperSystem.cs·Karma/
- **[Doc: Code]** RNG is a single System.Random + PushSeed stack, restoration on load unconfirmed (UNVERIFIED) — recorded as a cautionary example for determinism.

### 14.10 Brogue CE — A Real Implementation of Seed Determinism [REF:OS-BROGUE-RNG]

- **[Doc: Code]** Two ranctx, SUBSTANTIVE (gameplay) and COSMETIC (presentation), are initialized with the same seed, strictly isolated by presentation-scope macros, and rand_range uses rejection sampling (bias removal). src/brogue/Math.c
- **[Doc: Code]** Master seed → per-floor child seed table (stream swapped/restored during generation) — regenerating an earlier floor does not shift later floors. src/brogue/RogueMain.c
- **[Doc: Code]** Save = recording file (36B header: version·seed·turn·depth), and a 1-byte RNG checksum every turn detects desync immediately. The seed catalog diff serves as the CI regression oracle. src/brogue/Recordings.c·test/compare_seed_catalog.py
- **[Application Proposal]** Review PurposeRng stream naming, per-region child seeds, per-turn checksums, and seed catalog regression as implementation guidelines for the Janseon determinism contract.

### 14.11 NetHack — Conduct Counters and Bones [REF:OS-NETHACK-CONDUCT]

- **[Document: Code]** conduct is a counter of 16 violation counts — 'Jikim' (kept)=0, not a history recalculation. The prototype for accumulating cast deeds (abandoned companions, destroyed stations). include/you.h
- **[Document: Code]** RNG is split into CORE (game)/DISP (display) (ISAAC-64) — however, it has a `% x` bias, so when copying, the Brogue approach is recommended. src/rnd.c
- **[Document: Code]** Bones use the same serializer as regular saves, a 1/3 discovery chance, and sanitization of player-provided names — the prototype for the 'remnants of the fallen' event. src/bones.c

### 14.12 Zero-K — Real-Time Retreat, Formations, and Suppression [REF:OS-ZK-RETREAT]

- **[Document: Code]** Retreat is a unit state: thresholds 30/65/99% (HP ratio), moves to the haven (radius 160) and waits until fully healed, interrupted immediately by any other command. LuaRules/Gadgets/cmd_retreat.lua — a reference case for an individual unit retreat state.
- **[Document: Code]** Drag-line formation: ranks 0–3 (front line = lower rank), rank_gap 100, Hungarian assignment on a distance matrix (greedy if exceeded), group speed is the slowest unit's speed. LuaUI/Widgets/cmd_customformations2.lua — the numerical skeleton for editing residual-line formations.
- **[Document: Code]** Tactical AI constants: kiting `sageori-leeway` + 30-frame prediction, jink parallel 200/tangent 80, updates spread over 20 frames. unit_tactical_ai.lua
- **[Document: Code]** timeslow = suppression: slowdown proportional to the `slowDamage/health` ratio, capped at 50%, decaying 4% per second. An unseeded math.random for haven jitter is a determinism hole (not adopted; noted). unit_timeslow.lua
- **[Document: Code]** Separation of commands (queue: move/engage/patrol) and state (retreat threshold, AI on/off) — the prototype for 'formation editing = state, advance/retreat = command'. state_commands.lua

### 14.13 Mindustry — Two Layers: Strategy ↔ Real Time [REF:OS-MIND-SECTORS]

- **[Doc: Code]** The sector graph owns the saves, only battles in progress during occupation run in real time, and attacked sectors are frozen — the closest real implementation of Janseon's S/W/B connections. type/Sector.java·game/Universe.java
- **[Doc: Code]** Campaign turn is 120 s, unplayed base production is a 60-tick moving average×dt, and invasion probability is `1/100×(0.8+(injeopjeok-1)×0.3)` (injeopjeok = adjacent enemies; 20-minute grace period). Vars.java·Universe.java — the flaw that the invasion RNG is outside the seed is compensated for in Janseon.
- **[Doc: Code]** Pause = skip the simulation block (rendering/input maintained), and a delta clamp of 4 prevents jumps. Control.java·ClientLauncher.java
- **[Doc: Code]** Formation uses a shared offset buffer (center reference → circle fill 0.7 compression → physics push-out → destination raycast). Command queue cap is 50, and unit cap = sum of building modifiers (logistics). ai/UnitGroup.java·entities/Units.java

### 14.14 Warzone 2100 — Ranks, Command Radius, and Component Research [REF:OS-WZ-RANK]

- **[Doc: Code]** Experience is 16.16 fixed-point, and rank uses per-brain threshold tables (regular 0/4/8…512, command 0/24…2048), with -6% damage taken, +5% hit chance, and +5% speed per level — since these are judgment modifiers rather than HP increases, they coexist with persistent injury. src/droid.h·combat.cpp
- **[Doc: Code]** Secondary orders are a bitmask: retreat at 25%/50%/never + fire discipline + range mode, with the integer check `body×100 ≤ repairLevel×originalBody`. src/orderdef.h·order.cpp — prototype of the per-character 3-tier retreat policy.
- **[Doc: Code]** Command group capacity is `level×mult+base` (6+2×level), and the radius is a per-rank array r[level]² — experience sharing and modifiers apply only within the radius. src/cmddroid.cpp·droid.cpp — skeleton of the formation leader's command radius.
- **[Doc: Code]** Research unlocks components (componentResults) and units are component-combination templates — a card/equipment research-and-equip model. src/researchdef.h·droiddef.h

# 레퍼런스 게임 메커니즘 데이터베이스

> 이 문서는 게임 설계의 **근거 원천**이다. 레퍼런스 게임들의 위키·매뉴얼·개발자 블로그에서 확인된 메커니즘을 원문 인용과 함께 정리하고, 각 게임 로직 문서가 어떤 레퍼런스에서 어떤 규칙을 채택했는지 추적 가능하게 한다. 이 문서의 S-ID는 조사별 출처 색인을 사용하며 기존 Research-Sources 목록과는 별개다.
> 

## 사용법

- 각 섹션은 **게임 → 메커니즘 → 원문 근거 → 잔선 채택** 구조
- 게임 로직 문서(Campaign-Loop.md 등)에서 이 문서를 인용할 때는 `[REF:게임명-메커니즘]` 형식
- 새 조사 결과가 나오면 해당 게임 섹션에 추가 (append-only)
- **조합 규칙**: 여러 게임에서 같은 문제에 대한 다른 해법이 있으면 "선택지"로 병기하고 잔선의 선택 이유를 명시

## 1. 켄시 (K-시스템) — 떠돌이 생존과 정착 진행

> 공개 위키 금지 용어이므로 내부 설계에서만 "K-시스템"으로 지칭. 상세: 내부 종합 조사 문서 §I.

### 1.1 시작 조건 [REF:K-START]

- **13개 시작 시나리오**: 각각 다른 "결핍" 조합 — 인원 부족/자금 부족/장비 부족/세력 관계 부족. 빈곤은 하나의 난이도가 아니라 여러 종류의 결핍이다.
- **플레이어 세력은 시작부터 존재**: `Nameless`라는 세력명으로, 정착 전부터 정치적 행위자. "정착해야 세력이 된다"가 아님.
- **"너는 특별하지 않다"**: 세계는 플레이어 없이도 돌아감. 적도 서로 싸운다.
- **잔선 채택**: Game-Thesis.md "무명 인물" 채택. **추가 설계**: 시작 시나리오 다양화(결핍 축별 분화).

### 1.2 생존 압박 [REF:K-SURVIVAL]

- **신체**: 부위별 체력. 팔/다리 절단 가능. 치료에는 시간+의료품. 회복 가능한 실패를 고르는 것이 초반의 기술.
- **식량**: 캐릭터별 허기. 방치 시 쓰러짐 → 방치 지속 시 사망.
- **패배 ≠ 게임오버**: 죽는 대신 노예로 팔리거나 강도에게 약탈당하고 살아남음. 실패 후 재기가 핵심 루프.
- **잔선 채택**: 부상 시스템("중상→HP 감소")은 채택. 패배 시 노예/약탈은 비목표이나 "패배 후 재기" 정신은 채택.

### 1.3 떠돌이→정착 [REF:K-SETTLEMENT]

- **세 가지 상태**: ①완전 유랑(야영) ②도시 내 집(임시 거점) ③야외 전초기지(생산 거점). 각각 다른 이벤트 조건.
- **정착 시점**: 날짜가 아니라 준비(연구·자재)와 욕구(생산 필요성)가 결정.
- **정착 후**: 외교·침공·세금 발생. 권리도 늘지만 책임도 늘음.
- **잔선 채택**: `떠돌이 → 시설 이용권 보유 → 선택적 역 운영자` 3단계. **정착은 필수 승급이 아님.**

### 1.4 무소속 경제 [REF:K-NOMAD]

- **유랑자도 정치적 행위자**: 세력 관계·평판이 존재. 도시에서 쫓겨나지 않음(범죄 시 제외).
- **경제원**: 약탈·상인·의뢰·채굴. 기지 없이도 기술 습득 가능(책+연구 벤치 이용).
- **잔선 채택**: "고정 거점이 없어도 준비/회복/정산 가능" — 시설 이용권 개념으로 해결.

### 1.5 "무에서 시작"이 재미있는 이유 [REF:K-WHY-FUN]

- **자발적 목표 생성**: 튜토리얼 목표가 아니라 "배고프다→식량→돈→일거리"의 자연스러운 욕구 체인.
- **실패 지점**: 초반 정보 부족으로 어디서 무엇을 해야 할지 모르는 것. 지속적 위협으로 휴식 없는 게임.
- **잔선**: 의뢰 게시판이 욕구 체인의 시작점. 지속 위협은 원정/거점 왕복 리듬으로 완화.

> 상세: 내부 종합 조사 문서 §II.

### 2.1 출신(Origins) [REF:BB-ORIGINS]

- **15개 기원**: 각각 시작 보너스가 아니라 **회사의 장기 규칙**(고용 한계, 시작 장비, 특수 능력). `Sellsword`는 독립 기원이 아님.
- **잔선**: 시작 시나리오를 "결핍 축"으로 다양화 시 참조.

### 2.2 경제 압박 루프 [REF:BB-ECONOMY]

- **일급(Wages)**: 매일 크라운 지급. 못 주면 사기 하락 → 이탈. **돈이 자유를 사고, 자유를 유지하려면 다시 벌어야 함.**
- **식량**: 매일 소모. 종류별 부패 속도 존재.
- **수리·의약·탄약**: 장비 유지 비용이 지속적 압박.
- **잔선 채택**: 보급 시스템. **차이**: 잔선은 화폐가 아니라 소모품. "매 원정 시 소모되는 압박"은 동일.

### 2.3 로스터 ≠ 배치 [REF:BB-ROSTER]

- **로스터**: 전체 소대원(성장 가능). **배치**: 전투 투입 인원.
- **부상자 교체**: 부상자는 로스터에서 쉬고 예비 인원이 대신 출전.
- 현재 목표의 병력·배치 정원은 미정이다.

### 2.4 세계 진화·위기 [REF:BB-CRISES]

- **4종 위기**: 귀족 전쟁·언데드 침공·오크 침공·성전(Holy War, Blazing Deserts). 위기는 배경이 아니라 **고용 시장과 보급망의 변화**.
- **계약 유형 변화**: 위기 중에는 특정 계약 증가/감소.
- **미시적 세계 변화**: 정착지 상태(파괴/점령/해방)가 개별 정착지 단위에서 일어남.
- **잔선 채택**: Campaign-Progression.md 위기 시스템. **설계 필요**: 위기 종류·트리거·3역 범위에서의 최소 구현.

### 2.5 정착지 [REF:BB-SETTLEMENTS]

- **도시**: 대형. 시장·무기고·훈련소·신전. **마을**: 소형. 기본 시장. **요새**: 군사. 병영.
- **남의 도시를 연결해 자기 기반으로 씀**: 정착하지 않아도 정착지 네트워크가 회사의 기반.
- **잔선 채택**: 역별 시설 차등. **설계 필요**: 3역 각각의 시설 목록.

### 2.6 수행단(Retinue) [REF:BB-RETINUE]

- **18명 비전투 수행원**: 건물 없이 회사가 발전하는 방법. 상인·정찰병·재단사 등.
- **잔선 채택**: 향후 검토 — 전투원 아닌 지원 인력 시스템.

### 2.7 지형 비용 [REF:BB-TERRAIN]

- **이동 AP**: 평지 2AP, 험지 3AP, 늪 4AP, 고도 변화 +1AP.

## 3. 첫 번째 비교 대상 — 인물 중심 대전략

### 3.1 인물 존재감 [참조:인물]

- **상시 초상**: 상단 바에 항상 초상·특성·스트레스·자원 표시.
- **인물 카드**: 특성 툴팁, 의견, 관계, 비밀.

### 3.2 선택 투명성 [참조:선택]

- **이벤트 옵션**: 각 선택지에 비용/효과/확률 사전 표시. Will Happen / Has Happened 구분.
- **중첩 툴팁**: 값 위에 커서 → 그 값의 계산 근거 툴팁 (왜 이 값인가?).
- **잔선 채택**: 조우 화면 7의 3선택(비용/효과/위험) + "왜 불가?" 툴팁이 이에 해당.

### 3.3 지도 정보 모드 [참조:지도]

- **지도 모드**: 영토/외교/종교/문화 등 정보별 색상 전환.
- **잔선 채택**: 전략 노선도 S의 "정보 모드" — 세력권/통행권/위협도 표시 전환.

### 3.4 경고/현안 시스템 [참조:현안]

- **차단 경고**: 행동 불가 시 버튼 옆 붉은 표시.

### 8.1 필드·작전·교전 [REF:UO-MAPS]

- [문서] 어레인으로 탐색·대화·채집하는 필드, 여러 부대를 실시간/일시정지로 지휘하는 스테이지, 접촉 후 사전 작전대로 자동 진행되는 교전이 연결된다. 필드에도 낮·밤 시계가 있고, 스테이지는 제한시간과 본거지 방어를 갖는다. [S140; S141 pp.12,16,28,37]
- [추론] 이동 명령을 내리는 지도는 여행/작전 2종, 교전 표현까지 포함하면 3개 기능 표면이다. 국가 5개나 스테이지 총수를 지도 종류 수와 혼동하지 않는다. [S140-S141]
- [적용 제안] 잔선의 여행→전투→정산 왕복을 강화하되 별도의 자동 교전 화면을 추가할 필요는 없다. [S141; S165]

### 8.2 브레이브·훈장·명성의 분리 [REF:UO-RESOURCES]

- [문서] 브레이브(Valor)는 전장 적 격파·시설 해방 등으로 얻고 출격·전장 스킬에 쓴다. 훈장(Honors)은 퀘스트/납품에서 얻어 고용·편성 확충·승급에 쓰며, 명성(Renown)은 랭크에 따라 기능을 해금한다. 서로 다른 자원이다. [S141 pp.18,21,28,30]
- [문서] AP는 교전 중 능동 스킬, PP는 조건부 반응 스킬에 사용한다. 스태미나는 교전 후 작전 지속성에 관여하며 0일 때 이동이 불가능하다. 한국 위키의 '0이면 무방비' 문장은 같은 문서의 정정과 충돌하므로 휴식 중 무방비와 동일시하지 않는다. [S141 pp.28,37; S142 §7.4/§8]
- [적용 제안] 전투 AP, 하루 보급, 조직 성장 자격을 하나의 추상 자원으로 합치지 않는다. 다만 원작 자원 종류를 모두 잔선에 추가하지도 않는다. [S141; S165]

### 8.3 6칸에 최대 5명: 역할·표적·순서 [REF:UO-FORMATION]

### 8.4 해방→복구→자원 회수 [REF:UO-LIBERATION]

- [문서] 해방 후 시설을 이용하고 채집품 납품으로 복구한다. 수비병 지정 시 이후 스테이지 완료마다 자금·주변 채집품을 받는다. 수비병으로 둔 인물도 출격할 수 있다. [S141 pp.18,20]
- [추론] 수비병은 신생/삼국지의 전담 행정 인력과 같은 기회비용이 아니다. 해방이 곧 자율 국가 전쟁·세금 경영을 뜻하지 않는다. [S141 p.20; S142 §7.1]
- [적용 제안] 역 해방과 시설 재가동을 분리하되, 잔선은 현지 담당자의 원정 부재가 운영에 미치는 영향을 별도로 설계한다. [S165]

### 8.5 조건부 모집 [REF:UO-RECRUIT]

- [문서] 공식은 60명 이상의 고유 인물을 설명한다. 스토리 동행, 서브퀘스트, 특정 인물의 전장 대화, 과거 처분의 지연 효과, 투기장 도전, 별도의 범용 용병 고용을 구별한다. [S140-S144]
- [문서] 힐다는 프림과 전장 대화 후 완료·필드 수락이 필요하고, 가멜은 초반 석방 여부가 후반 합류에 영향을 준다. 리뷰 64명/위키 최대71명은 집계 범위 차이로 기록하며 전수 영입 수를 확정하지 않는다. [S142-S144]
- [적용 제안] 인물 합류를 전리품처럼 자동 지급하지 말고 관계·이전 선택·임무에 연결한다. [S144; S165]

## 9. 배너로드 (Mount & Blade 2) — 같은 클랜의 정치적 자격 변화

> 기본 싱글플레이 구조. War Sails/모드 제외. 출시 리뷰와 후속 공식 패치, 전용 위키를 교차 확인하며 최신 모든 퍽·일당·창건 조건을 보증하지 않는다. 상세 연구 §9. [S145-S153]

### 9.1 무소속→용병→봉신→왕국 [REF:MB-PROGRESSION]

- [문서] 클랜은 인물·가족·동료와 여러 파티를 포함하며 왕국은 여러 클랜을 포함한다. 위키상 T1/명성50에 용병, T2/명성150에 봉신 자격을 얻는다. 캠페인에는 가족·메인 퀘스트의 틀이 있고 Sandbox는 이를 생략한다. [S146-S147; S151 §5]
- [문서] 용병의 영향력은 계약 수입에 연결되고 봉신은 봉토·정책·군단 동원에 참여한다. 독립 클랜의 영지 보유와 왕국 선포는 구별한다. 공식 e1.7.0 공지는 총독 대화 창건을 설명하므로 Dragon Banner 퀘스트만이 창건 방법이라는 옛 가이드는 채택하지 않는다. [S149; S152]
- [추론] 이 순서는 강제 장 목록이 아니라 권한을 배우는 경로다. BB 역시 자유 샌드박스지만 지속 주체가 용병회사이며 배너로드는 클랜의 국가적 역할까지 바뀐다. [S97; S106; S146-S149]
- [적용 제안] 잔선은 용역 계약→통행/보급 협약→운영 위탁→선택적 자치의 권한 전이로 번역한다. [S165]

### 9.2 병종·급료·보급·성장 [REF:MB-PARTY]

- [문서] 일반 병사 승급은 영웅의 개별 퍽 성장과 다르다. 기병 승급에는 말/전투마를 추가로 소비한다. 일급과 식량, 음식 다양성의 사기 효과, 부상·전투 도주가 원정의 부담을 만든다. [S148; S151 §3.2/§4/§5.6]
- [문서] 6속성군×3기술=18기술이며 사용 경험을 쌓고 속성/집중 포인트로 학습 효율·범위를 조절한다. 기술 단계에서 퍽을 선택한다. 정찰·병참·의료·공병 담당자에게 서로 다른 역량이 필요하다. [S147-S148]
- [추론] 집중 포인트는 즉시 기술 레벨을 사는 돈이 아니다. 어떤 인물을 실제 어떤 일에 배치하는지가 성장 경로다. [S148]
- [적용 제안] 잔선의 전문 인력은 전투력 외에 복구·운송·의료로 파티 지속력을 바꾸어야 한다. [S165]

### 9.3 세계 지도·봉토·군단·공성 [REF:MB-KINGDOM]

- [문서/추론] 파티가 움직이는 전략/여행 통합 지도, 현지 탐색 공간, 직접 전투의 3종 기능 표면이다. 지역 상호작용은 메뉴로도 처리할 수 있다. 한국 자료는 84일/년을 설명하지만 실제 초 환산과 모든 메뉴의 자동정지 경계는 미검증이다. [S145-S146; S151 §7; S153]
- [문서] 봉토는 공성 기여만으로 자동 소유되지 않고 배분 투표/군주의 결정이 개입한다. 총독·시설·식량·번영·충성·치안과 연결 마을의 안전이 중요하다. [S146; S151 §6]
- [문서] 영향력으로 다른 클랜 파티를 군단에 부르고 결속을 보충한다. 자기 클랜 파티 호출은 영향력 예외다. 공성은 지도에서 캠프/장비를 준비한 뒤 성벽·문·사다리·공성 장비가 있는 직접 전투로 이어진다. [S149; S151 §4.2/§6.2]
- [적용 제안] 수비 책임·동료 분산·연결 봉쇄는 참조하되 대규모 1인칭 액션 전투를 추가하지 않는다. [S165]

### 9.4 공방과 상단 [REF:MB-ECONOMY]

- [문서] 직접 교역은 지역 가격 차를 이용한다. 공방은 원료→제품과 현지 수요/경쟁에, 상단은 실제 이동·거래·호위·포획 위험에 묶인다. 상단 일급과 거래 매출의 시점도 다르다. [S146; S150-S151]
- [문서] 출시 리뷰는 공방/상단의 수익 원인 설명과 직접 운영 선택이 얕다는 한계를 지적한다. '경제 기능이 있다'와 '모든 사업을 깊게 경영한다'는 별개다. [S146]
- [적용 제안] 잔선의 생산 시설/운송조는 고정 이자가 아니라 원료·노선·담당자·운영비의 손익으로 보여 준다. [S165]

## 10. 신장의야망 (信長の野望) — 신생의 인사·군수와 천상기의 성장

> 신생 2022 일본어 본편 매뉴얼을 주근거로 사용한다. 현행 영어 Awakening/PK 매뉴얼의 별도 공성·방어거점은 확장 규칙으로 분리한다. 천상기는 PC 계열이며 SFC 예외를 표시한다. 상세 연구 §10. [S154-S156]

### 10.1 군·성·도로와 시간 [REF:NA-MAPS]

- [문서] 72국 아래 군이 있고, 성이 소속 군의 병력·군량 중심이 된다. 군단은 여러 성을 묶어 위임하는 조직이다. 지리 구획과 행정 조직을 같은 계층으로 취급하지 않는다. [S154 3200/4200/8500]
- [문서/추론] 전국 지도에서 내정·행군·접촉전·공성, 별도 합전에서 실시간 부대/퇴로 지휘를 한다. 본편은 전략+합전 2종 지도이며 확장 공성을 소급 집계하지 않는다. [S154 3300/4100/7300/7400; S155]
- [문서] 진행/정지를 조절하며 행군은 일별 군량 소비, 수입은 월초, 논공행상은 3개월마다다. 천상기의 계절 턴과 다르다. [S154 3300/7100/8600]

### 10.2 신분과 직명·지행 [REF:NA-DELEGATION]

- [문서] 직할지 대관, 다른 성의 영주, 성주, 군단장은 역할이 다르다. 훈공으로 오른 신분이 맡을 수 있는 자리를 해금한다. 낮은 신분은 대관에서 경험을 쌓고, 영주/성주 재배치 자유도도 제도개신 정책으로 열린다. [S154 3200/5100/8100]
- [문서] 높은 신분에 낮은 자리를 주면 충성이 하락할 수 있다. 낮은 충성은 출분·성의 조기 항복·독단 철수 위험이며, 능력·상성은 개발·성 전력에 영향을 준다. 담당자가 없는 군은 개발되지 않는다. [S154 3200/4300/5100]
- [추론] 영토 확대→새 자리→공신 보상→개발/전력 증가가 성장 루프다. 인재 부족은 실제 확장 병목이다. [S154 5100/8600]
- [적용 제안] 역장·시설 책임자·순찰 지휘를 분리하고 담당자 공백과 위임 결과를 표시한다. [S165]

### 10.3 경제와 전쟁 준비 [REF:NA-ECONOMY]

- [문서] 농촌/관개→석고→군량·병력, 시장/상인 마을→금 수입이다. 금 상납과 달리 군량은 성별 재고다. 노력은 작업에 묶였다가 완료 후 회복하고 정책은 준비 기간과 월 유지비를 가진다. [S154 4100/4200/5100/8100]
- [문서] 목표 지정은 영주의 내정을 중단시키고 군비 준비로 전환한다. 임전 상태는 전력·휴대 군량을 늘린다. 성하 방침의 자율 건설은 직접 건설과 속도/비용이 다르다. [S154 5300/7100]
- [적용 제안] 동원 비용에 출진 시 물자뿐 아니라 중단된 생산과 현지 인력을 포함한다. [S165]

### 10.4 부대·공성·위풍 [REF:NA-WAR]

- [문서] 성주와 소속 영주가 부대 능력을 형성한다. 기마/철포 LV는 시설·정책·특성에 따른 공격 효과이며 천상기의 배타적 병과 선택과 같지 않다. 도로 폭과 군량 일수가 전개를 제한한다. [S154 4200/7100]
- [문서] 본편 공성은 포위/강공과 내구도 공방, 합전은 전멸 외에도 총사기·퇴로·다이묘 격파로 승리한다. 위풍은 인근 귀속·외교·충성까지 바꿀 수 있다. [S154 7200/7300/7400]
- [적용 제안] 전술 결과가 인접 역의 협력/통행에 영향을 주는 인과를 참고하되 승리 한 번으로 무조건 영토 전체를 지급하지 않는다. [S165]

### 10.5 천상기의 재능·교육·군단 [REF:NA-TENSHOKI]

- [문서] PC214성/SFC120성, 전략은 계절 1턴과 군단 행동력, 합전은 주변 최대9성 참여다. 정치·전투·지모의 현재 능력과 재능 한계를 분리하고 실무·교육·전쟁으로 성장시킨다. 병과 적성과 군마/철포 조달도 전력을 바꾼다. [S156 §2.1-2.5]
- [문서] 1군단 외 자치·방침과 해임/해체의 충성 비용, 군단장의 독립 위험이 있다. 금·쌀·성 개발·상인 거래는 확인했지만 농업/상업의 정확한 수입 계절·산식은 미확인이다. [S156 §2.5-2.8]
- [추론/적용 제안] 성장과 다성 정복의 빠른 피드백은 매력적이나 전투 성장 폭증은 비전투 인물을 무의미하게 만들 수 있다. 잔선은 현장 복구·의료·운송에도 유효한 숙련 경로를 둔다. [S156 §2.5; S165]

## 11. 태합입지전 (太閤立志伝) — 생업·신분·명령권의 분리

> 5 원작2004/DX2022 중 DX 공식 매뉴얼을 기준으로 한다. 공식960명은 플레이 가능한 전체 인물 풀이지 초기 전원해금이 아니다. 상세 연구 §11. [S157-S160]

### 11.1 출세는 강제 단일 트리가 아니다 [REF:TR-CAREER]

- [문서] 히데요시의 출세가 모티프지만 무사·상인·닌자·해적과 검호·다인·의사·대장장이의 목표가 다르다. 낭인/기존 직위 인물로 시작할 수 있으며 '농민→관백'은 공통 레벨 트리가 아니다. [S157; S158 1200; S159 4200/5160]
- [문서] 가로 이하에서는 주명을 수행하고 성주부터 직접 평정을 열어 부하에게 일을 준다. 국주는 복수 성·수송, 다이묘는 외교·정복 방향과 타 직능 세력 의뢰를 결정한다. 독립/계승은 단순 XP 자동 승급과 다르다. [S159 5100/5130/5160]
- [적용 제안] 생업 숙련·조직 직위·시설 운영권을 별도 축으로 두고, 의무원이 장군이 되지 않아도 진료소 운영이라는 성취를 갖게 한다. [S165]

### 11.2 기한과 귀환 보고 [REF:TR-TIME]

- [문서] 무사 평정은 홀수 달1-5일, 임무 선택→수행→기한 내 주군 보고→훈공이다. 남는 시간에 돈벌이·사사·교류를 한다. 임무 물품 확보만으로 보고가 완료되지 않는다. [S159 5100]
- [문서] 닌자/해적은 불규칙 소집 후 한 달 내 출석, 상인은 홀수 달 초 평정이다. 봉록은 월초 집 금고에 들어간다. 이동/수련/휴식이 일정의 기회비용을 만든다. [S158 3100/3200; S159 4200-4500/5200-5400]
- [적용 제안] 잔선의 운송·치료·복구 의뢰는 작업 완료와 귀환 보고, 다음 업무까지의 개인 시간을 구별한다. [S165]

### 11.3 사사·인맥·카드 [REF:TR-SKILLS]

- [문서] 5능력·16기능·6카드 범주를 구별한다. 사사는 높은 기능의 인물/시설과 관계·물품 조건에 연결되며 공식 설명상 레벨4까지 배운다. 수련/과업의 미니게임·자동 처리에는 판본 차이가 있다. [S158 3300/3400; S160 §3]
- [문서] 선물·다도·대련으로 친밀해지면 취업/사사/입문/모집의 접근이 열린다. 훈공·악명·칭호·관위는 친밀도와 다른 축이다. 주인공 카드는 다음 플레이 인물 해금이며 모든 기술 카드가 다음 회차 공용 전투력은 아니다. [S158 3200/3400/3600; S159 5100/5160/5500]
- [적용 제안] 교사·전문가를 찾아가는 여행과 생업 현장 실무를 성장에 연결한다. [S165]

### 11.4 비통치 경로와 개인 서사 [REF:TR-PATHS]

- [문서] 상인은 분점·판로·상업권 특권, 닌자/해적은 별도 거점·후원 다이묘·영역을 운영한다. 검호는 유파/도장/제자, 다인은 다실/다회, 의사는 약초·제약·처방·진료 평판, 대장장이는 기술 습득·원료·무구 제작을 추구한다. [S159 4300-5800]
- [문서] 세력 직업과 구도 직업은 병행할 수 있으나 집에 여는 작업장은 하나다. 개인전과 합전도 별개이며 합전에서는 신분에 따라 자기 부대 또는 군단 전체를 지휘한다. [S158 1200/3500/3600]
- [추론/적용 제안] '어떤 사람으로 살아왔는가'가 '누구에게 어떤 일을 맡길 권한이 생겼는가'로 이어져야 한다. 모든 성공을 군사 통일로 환산하지 않는다. [S158-S159; S165]

## 12. 삼국지 (三國志) — 14의 토지·담당자·보급선

> 2020 본편 군주제. 삼국지 8 REMAKE 등 전 무장 플레이 작품과 구별하며 '2026 최신 출시작'이라는 수식어를 쓰지 않는다. 상세 연구 §12-14. [S161-S164]

### 12.1 군주제·HEX·10일 실행 [REF:RTK-MAPS]

- [문서] 최소 도시를 가진 세력을 고르고 HEX→지역 중심(core)→도시권을 확보한다. 군단은 여러 도시의 위임 조직이다. 도시를 모두 잃으면 세력이 붕괴한다. [S162 2400/3100/3300]
- [문서/추론] 전쟁과 행정이 같은 연속 지도에서 진행된다. 전략 단계에서 명령을 정하고 진행10일→보고로 반복하며 일반 명령은 진행 중 변경할 수 없다. 월은3순, 수입은 월초, 보급은 매순이다. Adjutant로 지정된 무장의 전법 타이밍 개입은 예외로 구별한다. [S162 3200/3300/5300]
- [적용 제안] 잔선의 시간 계약을 먼저 정하고 실시간 정지형·예약실행형·수동 전술 턴을 혼합하지 않는다. [S165]

### 12.2 인재가 행정 용량이 된다 [REF:RTK-OFFICERS]

- [문서] 공식은1000+무장·150+개성, 한국자료는 기본 역사무장1000·46도시·340중요지점을 기술한다. DLC/편집/역사 집계 범위를 구분한다. [S161; S163]
- [문서] 지역·징병·훈련 담당자를 임명하고 그 사람이 출진/다른 일을 하면 효과가 감소한다. 지역 무담당은 계절 개발/치안 하락을 낳는다. 통솔·무력·지력·정치·매력의 행정 용도가 다르다. [S162 4200]
- [문서] 군주의 주의는 시정 부서 슬롯·비용 한도를 정하고, 배치한 무장의 정책이 다음 순부터 활성화된다. 군사에는 자격과 정책 비용 예외가 있다. [S162 4100]
- [적용 제안] 유명 전투원뿐 아니라 평범한 전문 인력도 시설·지역 운영에 필요하게 만든다. [S165]

### 12.3 개발·징병·진형·연계 [REF:RTK-WAR]

- [문서] 지역의 상업/농업/병영 개발, 도시 모집/훈련 담당을 나눈다. 병력 증가는 소비도 늘리고, 군량 부족은 병력 이탈/사기 저하를 낳는다. [S162 4200]
- [문서] 출진은 지휘관·진형·병력·전법·목표·접적/추격/퇴각 방침을 묶는다. 진형은 기동·점령 폭·부대전·공성을 구분하며 관직은 지휘 병력 상한에 연결된다. [S162 5100/6100/7100]
- [문서] 좋은 관계의 지휘관이 같은 군단에서 근접하고 상태 이상이 없으면 연계 능력/전법이 강화된다. 개성은 유불리와 일부 행동 설정 제한을 만든다. 영웅은 병력 숫자 배수만이 아니다. [S162 5100]

### 12.4 보급선과 외교의 버전 경계 [REF:RTK-SUPPLY]

- [문서] 원도시와 부대를 자국/동맹 통제 토지로 연결하고 길이·험지가 소비에 영향을 준다. 차단되면 큰 사기 손실과 이동/공격 제한을 받는다. 공식은 여포/장료를 정면 대결 대신 보급 차단·시설·전법으로 상대하라고 권한다. [S162 5100/7200]
- [문서] 본편 외교 목록은 친선·동맹·파기·포로 반환·공격 요청·항복 권고다. 범용 혼인동맹 명령은 확인되지 않았다. 역사 혼인/배우자 관계를 신생의 일반 혼인 외교와 혼동하지 않는다. [S162 6100; S154 6200]
- [적용 제안] HEX 색칠보다 역·터널·환승 보급 연결을 참조한다. 통행·펌프·전력·의료 이송의 복구가 작전 지속력을 바꾸게 한다. [S165]

### 12.5 5종 결합 원칙 [REF:RTK-SYNTHESIS]

- [추론] 유니콘은 해방에 따른 편성 선택지 확대, 배너로드는 클랜의 정치적 자격, 신생은 인사 위임, 태합입지전은 개인의 경력/권한, 삼국지14는 토지·행정·보급 연결을 성장의 중심으로 삼는다. 모두를 같은 '빈손→왕' 공식으로 묶을 수 없다. [S141; S146-S149; S154; S158-S159; S162]
- [적용 제안] 잔선의 중심은 BB 원정 손익+K 생존/회복 지속성+태합입지전 생업/직위 분리다. 유니콘의 상성/편성, 신생의 위임, 삼국지의 연결 차단은 그 중심을 보강한다. [S84; S89; S97; S102-S104; S141; S154; S158-S159; S162]
- [적용 제안] 유니콘의 '수비병도 출격 가능'과 신생/삼국지의 전담 인력 비용은 양립하지 않으므로 선택해야 한다. 잔선에서는 원정 시 대행 또는 운영 효율 손실을 권하며, 수치와 자격은 별도 설계다. 옛 청사진의 수동 SRPG·3역×B1/B2 계약은 바이블 2.5절 D3와 v3 09장 3절의 야전으로 대체됐고(위 v3 경계 참조), 이 연구는 그 전투 계약과 점령→안정화→통합 설계를 바꾸지 않는다. [S141 p.20; S154 5300; S162 4200; S165]
